title: Unify Foodworks Raises Rs 5 Cr In Seed Funding To Expand Moe’s And Carvel In India
summary: Unify Foodworks Raises Rs 5 Cr In Seed Funding To Expand Moe’s And Carvel In…
detailed: Unify Foodworks raised Rs 5 crore in a seed funding round through compulsorily convertible debentures.
The round included participation from Faad Capital, Atrium Angels, SailThru Ventures, and investor Arjun Vaidya.
The company is the exclusive pan-Indian master franchisee for Moe's Casa Mexicana and Carvel, which are owned by Roark Capital.
Fresh capital will fund store expansion across the National Capital Region with a long-term goal of opening over 100 stores in India.
sentences: Unify Foodworks, the exclusive pan-Indian master franchisee of Moe’s Casa Mexicana and Carvel, has raised Rs 5 crore in a seed funding round through compulsorily convertible debentures (CCDs).
The funding round saw participation from Faad Capital, Atrium Angels, SailThru Ventures and investor Arjun Vaidya, as per a media report.
The fresh capital will be used to expand the presence of both brands across the National Capital Region (NCR), where they made their India debut.
The company plans to increase store density, strengthen consumer recall and improve its operating model as it works towards building the brands into national restaurant chains.
Unify Foodworks has set a long-term target of opening more than 100 stores across India.
It also plans to strengthen its supply chain, logistics and store-level training as it prepares to expand beyond NCR.
Launched in November 2024 by Sumer Sethi, Unify Foodworks holds the exclusive pan-Indian master franchise rights for Moe’s Casa Mexicana, Carvel and Moe’s Southwest Grill.
Moe’s Casa Mexicana is the international evolution of US fast-casual restaurant chain Moe’s Southwest Grill, with India serving as its first international market.
Its menu includes burritos, bowls and tacos, along with India-focused offerings such as Habanero Paneer.
Carvel, an American ice cream brand founded in 1934, entered India in 2025 with its first outlet in Connaught Place, New Delhi.
Both brands are owned by US-based private equity firm Roark Capital, whose portfolio also includes Subway, Baskin-Robbins and Dunkin’.

As part of its expansion strategy, Unify Foodworks plans to use NCR as a testing ground for store economics, menu localisation and operational efficiency before replicating the model in other markets.
The company is focusing on building its operational capabilities and strengthening its distribution network to support its long-term expansion plans across India.
